title: Lean adipocyte oxylipin signaling restrains breast cancer through ferroptosis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded both GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) supplementary count tables for GSE300839 (625 KB and 804 KB gzipped) and parsed them: human matrix 61,552 genes x 12 samples, mouse matrix 56,980 genes x 18 samples, zero missing values, library sizes 18.5-31.1 million reads. Pulled all 30 sample records: 3 cell lines (SkBr3 human breast cancer, E0771 mouse breast cancer, NMuMG mouse normal mammary epithelium) x 3 treatments (control medium, lean-fat-cell secreted medium, obese-fat-cell secreted medium), 10 samples per treatment. Confirmed BioProject PRJNA1282180 is the same 'Transcriptome or Gene expression' submission.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the lipid measurements: the 9S-HODE (9S-hydroxyoctadecadienoic acid, an oxidized fatty acid) levels in human breast tissue, the inverse correlation with body mass index, the mouse tumour-growth experiments and the patient-derived organoid growth assays. Europe PMC returned HTTP 500 for the full text and the supplementary-file listing was not retrievable, so only the abstract and the repository metadata were readable; no mass-spectrometry deposit was found (Metabolomics Workbench search for this group returned nothing).

a1_downloadable.note: Both GSE300839 count tables downloaded anonymously from the NCBI (National Center for Biotechnology Information) FTP site and parsed on the first try; no login or application.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Treatment group (control / lean secretome / obese secretome) and cell line are explicit fields in the GEO sample records, so the label exists as metadata and does not need constructing.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are raw gene counts keyed by Ensembl gene identifiers, present in the files; no identifier lookups needed to build a feature matrix.

a4_units_stated.note: Files are headed 'raw_counts' with integer read counts per gene per sample; units unambiguous, though normalisation would be left to the user.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAILS. The unit of prediction is the sample, and there are only 30 (10 per treatment, 3-4 replicates per cell line x treatment cell). The checklist needs about 400 rows minimum for a classification task; 30 is an order of magnitude short. Genes are features, not independent examples.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; both matrices load into pandas in seconds.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO's stated design (E0771, SkBr3, NMuMG under control / lean / obese secretome) matches the 30 sample records and the two matrices exactly.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label is the experimenter-assigned treatment condition, a physical intervention, not a model output and not derivable from the count features except through the biology we would be modelling.

honest_claim_h3: Not applicable: with 10 samples per treatment group and 3 cell lines, any classifier trained here would be describing 30 observations, not making a claim that generalises.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a breast cell's gene expression to tell whether it was bathed in fluid from lean or obese fat cells.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example is one cultured breast cell sample described by read counts for about 57,000-62,000 genes; there are 30 such samples in total, which I counted in the downloaded files.
plain_idea.predict: Which of three culture conditions the sample came from - plain medium, medium conditioned by lean mouse fat cells, or by obese mouse fat cells - a label assigned by the experimenters when they set up the dishes.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: If it worked, a transcriptional signature of 'obesity-conditioned' tumour cells could be looked for in human tumour datasets; but with 30 samples the result would be a description of this one experiment, not a transferable signature.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: classify breast cell RNA-sequencing profiles by whether they were exposed to lean or obese adipocyte (fat cell) secretions, or derive a ferroptosis (iron-dependent cell death) response signature from the differential expression. The deposited data is 30 bulk RNA-sequencing samples, which supports standard differential-expression statistics but not machine learning.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the actual downloads: 1.4 MB gzipped total, both matrices parsed in pandas in under five seconds on this laptop.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the samples in the GEO series - 30, with 10 per treatment group. That alone kills it, and it takes one request.

verdict_reason: Part A5 fails: the only deposited data is 30 bulk RNA-sequencing samples (10 per treatment, 3 cell lines), far below the ~400 needed for classification. The paper's quantitative lipid and tumour measurements, which are the interesting part, are not deposited anywhere I could find - no Metabolomics Workbench entry, and Europe PMC returned errors for the full text and supplement, so those numbers exist only in figures. Clean, honest, well-labelled data; simply a lab-scale experiment, not an ML dataset.
